annotations.annotation_text: The introduction to the 'Willingdone Museyroom', which serves simultaneously as the Wellington Monument in Phoenix Park, the National Museum of Ireland, and a giant midden heap. It meta-textually represents the Wake itself as a repository of historical fragments.
sources: FWEET: Finnegans Wake Extensible Elucidation Treasury. http://fweet.org/

annotations.annotation_text: Kate the cleaner acts as the tour guide, warning visitors (readers) of the low entryway. This establishes the structural metaphor of entering a burial mound or ancient tumulus.
sources: FWEET: Finnegans Wake Extensible Elucidation Treasury. http://fweet.org/

annotations.annotation_text: The Duke of Wellington ('Willingdone') emerges as a surrogate for HCE. As an Irish-born British hero, he embodies the theme of empire-building and the masculine historical figure who must inevitably fall.
sources: FWEET: Finnegans Wake Extensible Elucidation Treasury. http://fweet.org/

annotations.annotation_text: A reference to the Magazine Fort in Phoenix Park. The tour maps Waterloo topography onto Dublin landmarks, conflating military defense with domestic architecture.
sources: FWEET: Finnegans Wake Extensible Elucidation Treasury. http://fweet.org/

annotations.annotation_text: A multi-layered motif. The tour guide solicits a gratuity, but 'tip' also refers to a rubbish tip (midden), pointing to the Wake's nature as a chaotic dump of history, and the sound of the falling giant.
sources: FWEET: Finnegans Wake Extensible Elucidation Treasury. http://fweet.org/

annotations.annotation_text: The Prussians, specifically Blücher, arriving at Waterloo. In the Museyroom's domestic drama, historical forces are reduced to squabbling neighbors or rival suitors.
sources: FWEET: Finnegans Wake Extensible Elucidation Treasury. http://fweet.org/

annotations.annotation_text: The sound of Wellington's famous horse, Copenhagen. The horse represents the animal vitality of the empire builder, echoing the equestrian statues of Dublin.
sources: FWEET: Finnegans Wake Extensible Elucidation Treasury. http://fweet.org/

annotations.annotation_text: Napoleon's famous quote about making marmalade of Wellington's troops is domesticized. War is translated into kitchen squabbles, reducing the epic to the mundane.
sources: FWEET: Finnegans Wake Extensible Elucidation Treasury. http://fweet.org/
